references.text: The people's reaction when they saw the pillar of cloud at the entrance to the tent, showing their reverence for God's presence as Moses went to the tent.
The people rose and stood at the entrance to their tents, a similar action demonstrating respect and attention.
The context concerning the tent of meeting that Moses set up outside the camp, where everyone who sought the Lord would go out.
The Lord revealed Himself in the pillar of cloud at the entrance to the tent, showing the same pattern of divine presence at the tent.
The Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance to the tent, parallel to Moses' visit to the tent of meeting.
Both describe the entire congregation gathered at the entrance to the tent of meeting in expectation of God's revelation.
A direct narrative parallel where the congregation gathers at the entrance to the tent by Moses' command.
Contrast reference: The same position at the tent entrance expresses either respect (Ex 33) or complaint and God's anger (Num 11).
Clear theological contrast: Gathering at the tent as an expression of devotion (Ex 33) versus rebellion (Num 16).
Complementary events: The people waiting for Moses' entrance (Ex 33) and God's glory appearing at his exit (Lev 9).
